nodes.name: Arch Cummin
nodes.note: Venture capitalist. Owned Little St. James before Epstein; listed it in 1997 and sold it in 1998 (AP, via Axios; Newsweek). No other documented tie to Epstein.

nodes.name: Christian Kjaer
nodes.note: Danish investor whose family held Great St. James for almost four decades. Reported to have refused to sell to Epstein; the sale to Great St. Jim LLC closed on 28 Jan 2016 for $22.5M, with the buyer presented as tied to Sultan bin Sulayem (Miami Herald, via Fox News). Bin Sulayem had refused the use of his name (same report).

nodes.name: Bruce King
nodes.note: Former governor of New Mexico (d. 2009). His family sold Zorro Ranch to Epstein in 1993, reportedly for about $12M (KRQE, AP, as cited by Wikipedia). No other documented tie on this map.

nodes.name: Michael Daffey
nodes.note: Former Goldman Sachs executive. Bought 9 East 71st Street from the estate in March 2021 for $51M; the proceeds went to the estate and the victims' compensation fund (Forbes).

nodes.name: Todd Michael Glaser
nodes.note: Palm Beach developer. Bought 358 El Brillo Way from the estate in January 2021 for $18.5M, demolished the house and resold the lot for $26M (Forbes).

nodes.name: Georgi Tuchev
nodes.note: Bulgarian packaging businessman. Bought 22 Avenue Foch, Paris, from the estate in June 2022 for about $10M (Forbes).

nodes.name: 11 East 71st Street
nodes.note: Townhouse next to 9 East 71st. 1988: held by a corporation registered at Wexner's address, with Epstein as vice-president; 1992: moved to an Epstein-named trust; 1996: sold to another trust for $6.2M; 1998: bought by Howard Lutnick for $7.6M (Forbes, as cited by Wikipedia). Lutnick's own account is that he was a neighbour.

nodes.name: 5025 East Dublin Granville Rd, New Albany, Ohio
nodes.note: Bought by Epstein in 1993 for $3.5M; sold in 1998 for $8M to HHD & B LLC, a company linked to Wexner's New Albany Company (Forbes). Named in Maria Farmer's lawsuit.

nodes.name: 7558 King George Dr, New Albany, Ohio
nodes.note: Bought by Epstein in 1994 for $365,000; deeded in 2007 for $0 to a trust for Abigail Wexner, which sold it in 2011 for $365,000 (Forbes). The trust is a separate party; nothing here is a finding about any person.

nodes.name: HHD & B LLC
nodes.note: Bought 5025 East Dublin Granville Rd from Epstein in 1998 for $8M; linked to Wexner's New Albany Company (Forbes).

nodes.name: Trust for Abigail Wexner
nodes.note: Received 7558 King George Dr from Epstein for $0 in 2007 and sold it in 2011 (Forbes).

nodes.name: Elizabeth Ross (Libet) Johnson
nodes.note: Johnson & Johnson heiress (d. 2017). In 1998 put her Vail chalet into a revocable trust with Epstein, then her financial adviser, as co-trustee (notarized deed; People).

nodes.name: Vail chalet (Johnson trust)
nodes.note: Built 1996; held from Aug 1998 by Libet Johnson's revocable trust with Epstein as co-trustee; sold by the trust after her death, for about $24M (People). Not an Epstein property.

nodes.name: Vila Olímpia flat, São Paulo
nodes.note: Two-bedroom flat bought by Epstein on 5 May 2003 for R$245,000 and sold on 1 Aug 2005 for R$179,300 (property record obtained by BBC News Brasil). A Brazilian taxpayer number in his name dates from 2003.

nodes.name: Four rented flats, Kensington and Chelsea, London
nodes.note: Rented by Epstein to house women; six who lived there later said they were his victims. At least 53 Eurostar tickets bought for women 2011-19, 33 after Giuffre's 2015 complaint, which the Metropolitan Police chose not to investigate (BBC, April 2026).

nodes.name: Bin Ennakhil palace, Marrakesh (attempted purchase)
nodes.note: Talks from 2011; Southern Trust agreed to buy through realtor Marc Leon in March 2019. Schwab wires of €11.15M (26 Jun 2019, reversed) and $14.95M (4 Jul, cancelled 9 Jul at Kahn's request). Schwab filed a suspicious-activity report on 13 Jul 2019. Never completed; since sold to another buyer (Reuters).

nodes.name: Comparison case: North Fox Island (Lake Michigan, 1970s)
nodes.note: Private island bought in 1960 by Francis Shelden, used in the 1970s by a ring operating behind a tax-exempt boys' charity (Brother Paul's Children's Mission, 1975). An associate was convicted in 1976 and testified to a US Senate subcommittee in 1977; Shelden left for the Netherlands, was never prosecuted and died there in 1996. No documented connection to Epstein: recorded only as a comparison of method.

node_notes.lsj: Bought in April 1998 from venture capitalist Arch Cummin by L.S.J. LLC, whose sole member was Epstein, for $7.95M (AP). Sold in 2023 with Great St. James for $60M to Stephen Deckoff for a resort; half the proceeds to a USVI trust for victims.
node_notes.gsj: Bought by Great St. Jim LLC on 28 Jan 2016 for $22.5M from Christian Kjaer, whose family had held it for almost four decades and who had refused to sell to Epstein; the buyer was presented as tied to Sultan bin Sulayem, who had refused the use of his name (Miami Herald). Later permits showed Epstein as the sole member. Sold in 2023 with Little St. James.
node_notes.zorro: About 7,600 acres near Stanley, bought in 1993 from the family of former governor Bruce King, reportedly for about $12M, plus about 1,200 acres leased from the state land office. State case closed 2019 at federal request; reopened Feb 2026; searched Mar 2026; legislature formed a truth commission. Sold 2023 to the Huffines family (San Rafael Ranch LLC).
node_notes.palm_beach: 358 El Brillo Way, bought 1990 for $2.5M. Site of the 2005 police investigation (more than 30 underage victims identified). Sold by the estate Jan 2021 for $18.5M to developer Todd Michael Glaser; demolished.
node_notes.nyc_house: Townhouse, about 21,000 sq ft. Bought by Wexner in 1989 for about $13M; Epstein lived there from about 1995 and bought it in 1998 for $20M, paid in instalments to 2000; title to Maple Inc. in 2011. Sold March 2021 for $51M to Michael Daffey.
node_notes.paris_apt: 22 Avenue Foch, bought 2001 for about $3.2M. Listed in the estate at $8.7M; sold June 2022 to Georgi Tuchev for about $10M.
